newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper charts seen pointing lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper charts seen pointing lower.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper's recent failure to hurdle stiff resistance leaves it vulnerable to the downside, with key support around $2,350 a tonne, chartists said on Wednesday.
But the market is jumpy and unpredictable ahead of the July traded options declaration.
Aluminium, aided by uptrending indicators and Tuesday's positive close, could take a look at resistance around $1,630.
COPPER - Unconstructive technicals have left the market at risk to downside moves as the market nervously awaited the July options declaration, analysts said.

"Looks vulnerable on the charts as the moving averages trend downwards and stiff resistance is evident above $2,440, compounded by the poor close below the $2,400 level," brokers Brandeis said in a report.
Support was expected at the recent low of $2,355.
The options declaration later in the day was expected to be lively, with fluctuations in the spread potentially bringing key strikes into play, analysts said.
At 0800 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,385/$2,389, off Tuesday's $2,393 afternoon kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - After filling a chart gap between $1,608 and $1,612 in late trading on Tuesday, aluminum was targeting the high of $1,628 dating from June 11, analysts said..
"Work done around $1,600 should now become support, but real support is in the $1,580 area," said the daily aluminium report from LME brokers Gerald.
Three months aluminium was quoted at $1,612/15 per tonne at 0800 GMT, compared to $1,603 at Tuesday's kerb close.
